findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Observed the bar handwashing sink to be missing soap. CORRECTED: Staff was notified and soap was added. Ensure that handwashing sinks have a supply of soap.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. [P]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment:
Observed the following foods stored without covering:
(i) Breaded meat stored in a deep freezer without a cover, and the deep freezer had significant ice buildup. CORRECTED: Notified PIC that the meat item must be wrapped or covered before being stored in the deep freezer. PIC noted that in the past they were put in containers. PIC had staff wrap those items in plastic wrap.
(ii) Cut cake stored in a standing cooler without a cover beneath several different food items. CORRECTED: Notified a staff member and a lid was added.
Ensure food is protected from cross-contamination through wrappings, packaging, and covers.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(4) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (4) Except as specified under Subparagraph 3-501.15(B)(2) and in (B) of this section, storing the food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings. [C]

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Observed raw shrimp stored over pickle spirals in the pizza prep cooler. CORRECTED: Staff was notified and moved the contents of the cooler around so that all fish items were on the bottom shelf and all RTE foods were on the top shelf. Ensure that food is protected from cross-contamination by keeping RTE items stored above raw animal proteins in case of drips.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(1) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (1) Except as specified in (1)(d) below or when combined as ingredients, separating raw animal FOODS during storage, preparation, holding, and display from: (a) Raw READY-TO-EAT FOOD including other raw animal FOOD such as FISH for sushi or MOLLUSCAN SHELLFISH, or other raw READY-TOEAT FOOD such as fruits and vegetables, (b) Cooked READY-TO-EAT FOOD, and (c) Fruits and vegetables before they are washed; (d) Frozen, commercially processed and packaged raw animal FOOD may be stored or displayed with or above frozen, commercially processed and packaged, ready-to-eat food. [P]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed that the interior baffle of the ice machine had an accumulation of soil residues. Notified PIC that the ice machine needs to be kept clean to sight and touch, including the interiors. Ensure the ice machine is cleaned with enough frequency to keep it clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed an accumulation of grease and soil residues in the kitchen ventilation hood. Inspector notes that the last professional cleaning was 12 November 2025, with a note that the next cleaning should be in 6 months, which was 4 months ago. Please clean the hood to remove the accumulation of grease and soil residues before it can fall into food or cause a fire. Ensure that nonfood-contact surfaces are kept free of accumulated soil residues through frequent cleaning.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the bottom of the prep cooler in the kitchen near the kitchen window has an accumulation of water in the bottom. Staff noted that they vacuum it regularly, but it keeps coming back. Ensure that is repaired by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed that the kitchen sanitizer bucket (Chlorine) was at a concentration considered toxic (over 200ppm). CORRECTED: PIC and staff were informed and educated about better procedure to make a safer and still effective chlorine sanitizer concentration (1 cap of bleach per bucket to get 50-200ppm of Chlorine). Staff remade the sanitizer bucket and it tested at 100ppm (Chlorine). Ensure that sanitizers are made per manufacturer’s instructions and tested to ensure the levels are at a safe and effective concentration.
findings.citation_text: 7-202.12(A) Conditions of Use. POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS shall be: (A) Used according to: (1) LAW and this Code, (2) Manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and, for a pesticide, manufacturer's label instructions that state that use is allowed in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, (3) The conditions of certification, if certification is required, for use of the pest control materials, and (4) Additional conditions that may be established by the REGULATORY AUTHORITY.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13 Nonfood-Contact Surfaces. NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed.
findings.comment: Inspectors observed significant amounts of water to be leaking/ponding throughout facility. Areas mainly include walk in cooler, dry storage, and dish room. Per CK, kitchen will be closing until a plumber is contacted and leak is serviced.
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Other Liquid Wastes and Rainwater. Condensate drainage and other nonSEWAGE liquids and rainwater shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to LAW.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the kitchen sanitizer solution was at 0 ppm (Cl) when the inspector tested the bucket. The PIC was informed and they dumped and remade the bucket which tested at 150 ppm (Cl). Ensure that sanitizing solutions are always testing at the correct concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: Observed the can opener blade had an accumulation of debris. The PIC cleaned the blade to sight and touch during the inspection. The inspector educated that the can opener blade must be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after every use. Ensure that food contact surfaces are always clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: Observed the walk-in cooler fans have an accumulation of dust. Non-food contact surfaces must be cleaned at a frequency necessary to avoid the accumulation of dust, dirt, food residue, and other debris. Ensure that the walk-in cooler fans are cleaned to sight and touch by the next routine inspection.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There was a bottle of ranch and a container of pulled pork in the prep cooler that was observed to be past the date that it was date marked for. CORRECTED- Both items were discarded and the PIC was educated. Ensure that food is discarded if it exceeds the date that it is date marked with or the manufacturer’s expiration date, whichever comes first.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: There was not any sanitizer made and available to clean food contact surfaces. CORRECTED- A bucket was made using bleach and tested at the correct concentration. PIC was educated. Ensure that there is always sanitizer available during all times of food preparation to make sure that food contact surfaces are being properly cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Proper eating, tasting, drinking, or tobacco use
findings.comment:
2-401.11: Inspector observed a cup of soda on the sandwich make table. The drink was moved down on the shelf under the table next to the stove top. Store drinks properly in the kitchen. Properly wash hands after taking a break to drink. Maintain this violation corrected for the next routine inspection.  

 (A) EMPLOYEE SHALL eat, drink, or use tobacco in designated areas away from FOOD and FOOD-RELATED areas. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEE may drink from closed BEVERAGE Container if handled to prevent: (1) hands (2) container (3) FOOD and FOOD-RELATED ITEMS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: Inspector observed the hand sink in the kitchen to be blocked with a cart and a table. The cart was removed and the sink made accessible again. Also, a spoon was observed in the sink. The spoon was removed. Do not use the hand sink for any puropse other then handwashing. The violaitons were corrected at the time of inspection. Develope good habits and maintain the hand sink accessible at all times. 

(A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: Sausage in the pizza make table top is holding at 49F and Chicken held in the bottom is 53F to 58F internally. Chicken tenders, breast pieces and wings were voluntarily discarded along with two #10 cans of pizza sauce, five pounds of mozzarella cheese and one pound of cooked sausage. Other random items from the make table were also voluntarily discarded. The facility is going to order a new make table. In the interim they are going to use ice to hold food in the make table during busy times. Otherwise they will leave pizza toppings in the walk in cooler. 

(A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.comment:
4-301.11: The pizza make table has an independent thermometer which reads 55F.  Repair or replace the make table. Owner stated that the make table is going to be replaced. 

EQUIPMENT for cooling and heating FOOD, and holding cold and hot FOOD, shall be sufficient in number and capacity to provide FOOD temperatures.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: The floor drain near the kitchen hand sink is soiled. Clean and maintain the area free of accumulated soil. 

 (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Before open today, inspector observed the soda gun at the bar to have some accumulation of soil.  Inspector pointed this soil out to the bartender and the soda gun was washed rinsed and sanitized before open. The violation is considered corrected on site.

4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.comment:
3-307.11: FOOD shall be protected from contamination that may result from a factor or source not specified under Subparts 3-301-3-306. 

Inspector observed that cooks are wearing tank tops in the kitchen. The kitchen is not overly hot at this time and they do not appear to be sweating. Food preparation staff needs to wear clothing items that will protect food from potential contact with perspiration. Properly protect food.

findings.title: Proper reheating procedures for hot holding
findings.comment:
3-403.11: (A) TCS FOOD cooked, cooled, and reheated shall be reheated to 165F for 15 seconds. (P) (B) If reheated with microwave, FOOD rotated, stirred, covered, and allowed to stand for 2 minutes covered. (P) (C) Commercially processed FOOD shall be reheated to 135F. (P) (D) Reheating may not exceed 2 hours.(P) (E) Unsliced portions of MEAT roasts may be reheated according to oven parameters and minimum TCS conditions. (C)  
At approximately 11:15am, the facility had cheese sauce and house made marinara on the hot well at 109F and 85F respectively. The foods were not ready to serve. The facility opens for service at 11am. The items had been in the hot holding unit for less than an hour. Temperature on hot well unit was turned up. The house marinara came up to 165F on it’s own in the hot well  before it was served.  The cheese sauce was removed from the hot holding well and placed on a double boiler to bring the cheese sauce up to 165F. Highly suggest reheating on the stove top before placing food in the hot holding well for service.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Observed in use utensils stored on a plate next to the food being stirred. Store in use utensils properly according to the rule above. Utensils were moved into the food.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
6-501.18: PLUMBING FIXTURES such as HANDWASHING SINKS, toilets, and urinals shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. 

The tank of the toilet in the restroom to the right has soil on it along with soil in the toilet. Clean and maintain fixtures free of accumulated soil.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the only allergen training certification available to be expired. See that all CFPM’s have up-to-date allergen certification (valid for 3 years). Print copies for the public health binder. Discussed with PIC. Ensure by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the soda nozzle to have a build-up of mold and debris. Observed the ice machine (serviced by Bormida) to have mold along the interior baffle. Discussed with PIC. PIC began to clean both areas during the inspection. Ensure staff is aware to soak/clean the soda nozzles and soda nozzle holders routinely. Ensure staff is aware to periodically check the interior baffle of the ice machine for mold debris. COS.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (2) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 41F or less. (B) EGGS not treated to destroy Salmonellae shall be stored at 45F or less. 

Observed the pizza prep cooler is be out of temperature. Majority of foods were ~47-51 degrees F. Lunch rush had just occurred and prep cooler was opened frequently which could have contributed to the higher temperatures. Probed temperatures included: shred cheese (47 degrees F), raw chicken (50 degrees F), sausage (51 degrees F). Fish, raw chicken were voluntarily discarded. PIC stated most of the other items were pulled from the walk-in cooler and/or prepped that morning. The rest of this prep cooler was carted into the walk-in cooler to rapidly cool to under 41 degrees F. PIC called service man during inspection and he is scheduled to come tomorrow to repair the prep cooler. Repair man thought it may be a leak. PIC will call Inspector tomorrow to update on the status of the prep cooler. Do not use this prep cooler until repaired and holding temperatures under 41 degrees F consistently, even during a busy lunch rush. Inspector will follow-up on 9/2/22 or before.

findings.title: Approved thawing methods used
findings.comment:
3-501.13: TCS FOOD shall be thawed: (A) at 41F or below in refrigeration (B) completely submerged under running water, not getting above 41F (water temp of 70F or below). If food will be cooked, not getting above 41F for more than 4 hours. (C) part of the cooking process (D) Using any procedure if RTE FOOD is thawed and prepared for immediate service (E) ROP FISH that bear label shall be removed from packaging before thawing under refrigeration, upon completion of thawing from running water. 

Observed improper thawing of ground beef. Ground beef was in a basin of cold water thawing. Cease practice. Thawing should occur in refrigeration under 41 degrees F or completely submerged in running water and not having a temperature above 41 degrees F. Discussed with PIC. PIC indicated an employee had done this before lunch rush. Discuss proper thawing techniques with staff. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.112: Dead or trapped birds, insects, rodents, and other pests shall be removed from control devices and the PREMISES at a frequency that prevents their accumulation, decomposition, or the attraction of pests. 

Observed the sticky fly strip to be full of flies (away from food contact surfaces). Discussed frequent changes with PIC. Flies are usually in the facility in the summer due to the large sliding doors going outside to the sand volleyball. People frequently come in and out and flies are let in. There is a fly light as well as the fly strip which appears to be hindering flies in the kitchen. PIC removed the full fly strip and is replacing it. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning:
1. Walk-in cooler fan has accumulation of dust.
2. Oven in the kitchen has an accumulation of baked/black food debris and splash at the base of the oven. PIC indicated oven is rarely used; however, a deep cleaning would be advisable in case of use.
3. Pizza oven has large amount of food debris on the base.

Ensure frequent cleaning of non-food contact surfaces. Clean by next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following places in need of repair:
1. There are numerous holes in the wall to the right of the hand sink in the kitchen. Caulk the holes to make area smooth and easily cleanable.
2. The shelving of the dry storage is in need of re-painting in areas (paint as come away from the particle board). Repaint the areas of the shelving that are in need of repair.
3. The grates of the reach-in cooler across from the bar have rusted and paint is coming away. Replace the shelving grates in the cooler and/or repaint the grates so they are smooth and easily cleanable and prevent paint flakes from chipping.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Repair before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the wooden piece added to the kitchen door to not be sealed. Seal wood piece with a sealant or paint. Discussed with PIC. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to have 0-10 ppm of bleach after multiple runs and testing. Machine is not pulling bleach correctly. Facility has test strips to check bleach concentration of dish machine. PIC called for a service repair. Inspector instructed facility to use 3 compartment sink until repaired - wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 11/1/21.

Observed both sani buckets in the kitchen to have 0 ppm of bleach. Employee was not utilizing bleach but dish soap containing bleach within the buckets. Inspector discussed utilizing concentrated bleach in the sani buckets. Buckets were correct - 200 ppm each. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed several items to be expired past the 7 day date marking system:
1. Multiple containers of pre-portioned sauces and dressings within the reach-in cooler near the bar (blue cheese, Italian dressing, thousand island, etc.) - dated 10/26.
2. Taco meat, grinder mix, and bacon within the bottom prep cooler #2 - dated 10/27.
3. Marinara within the walk-in cooler - dated 10/28.

Food items were voluntarily discarded. Ensure staff is going through the coolers to discard outdated foods. Discussed with PIC and employees within the kitchen. COS.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple flies in the kitchen. This was a problem during the last routine inspection on 7/23/21. Fly control box in the back dish machine area appeared to be turned on. Ensure fly control methods such as a fly strips (away from food-contact areas). Inspector will follow-up on 11/8/21.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed the chest freezer in the back dry storage area and the reach-in freezer along the kitchen prep line to have an accumulation of frost and ice. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 12/16/19, 6/25/20, and 7/23/21.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. 

(REPEAT) Observed the men’s toilet room door to not be self-closing. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 7/23/21. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple areas of the facility that were found in a state of disrepair and are no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulk of women’s hand sink is in need of repairs. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection son 12/16/19, 6/25/20, and 7/23/21. 
2. Trim is not present around the inside dry storage door. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/25/20 and 7/23/21.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Observed food handler to enter kitchen, wash hands correctly, but turn off the faucet without a barrier such as a paper towel. Discussed proper hand washing with employee. An IDPH proper hand washing sign is posted above this hand sink. Ensure proper hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-202.15: (A) Outer openings of FOOD ESTABLISHMENT shall be protected against entry of insects and rodents. (B) Does not apply to FOOD ESTABLISHMENTS which opens into larger structure. (C) Exterior doors need not be self-closing if designed for limited-use. (D) If opening present, opening shall be protected against rodent and insects. (E) Paragraph (D) not applicable when pests are absent. 

Observed back door in the kitchen to have seal missing around the door, mainly the bottom. Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure seal is replaced on door in order to hinder pests. Correct by next routine inspection.

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.comment:
6-501.111: PREMISE shall be maintained free of insects, rodents, and other pests. If present (A) Routinely inspect shipments of FOOD and supplies (B) Inspect PREMISE routinely (C) Using methods, such as trapping devices Pf (D) Eliminate harborage conditions. 

Observed multiple flies throughout the kitchen. Door to kitchen is broken and does not shut (off hinges). Fly control box on the back dish machine area wall appeared to be off. Ensure fly control methods such as this box and/or fly strips. Inspector will follow-up on 8/2/21.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-901.11: After cleaning and SANITIZING, EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS: (A) shall be air dried or used after adequate draining before FOOD contact. (B) May not be cloth dried except that UTENSISL that have been air-dried may be polished with cloths that are clean and dry. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple stacks of cups at the bar to be stacked wet. Ensure cups are air dried before stacking. Discussed practice with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/25/20.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-101.19: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other FOOD soiling or that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a CORROSION-RESISTANT, nonabsorbent, and SMOOTH material. 

(REPEAT) Observed the chest freezer in the back storage area and the reach-in freezer at the kitchen prep line to have accumulation of frost and ice. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/25/20 and 12/16/19.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: (A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. 

Observed no sani bucket present in kitchen. Food prep and lunch service was occurring and had been for some time. Discussed with PIC that a sani bucket must be prepared before food prep. Ensure it is routinely changed to keep sanitizer concentration appropriate. Food handler made a sani bucket upon Inspector’s request - 50 ppm. COS.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.comment:
5-205.15: A PLUMBING SYSTEM shall be: (A) Repaired according to LAW; P and (B) Maintained in good repair. 

(REPEAT) Observed leak at dish machine. A tray was present under the dish machine with a large amount of water within. Discussed repairs with PIC. Repair according to Illinois and local plumbing code. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 6/25/20.

findings.title: Toilet facilities: properly constructed, supplied, & cleaned
findings.comment:
6-202.14: Toilet rooms located on PREMISES shall be completely enclosed and provided with tightfitting and self-closing door. 

Observed men’s toilet room door is not be self-closing. This was noted in the general comments of the last routine inspection on 6/25/20. Repairs have not been conducted. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Multiple areas of the facility were found in a state of disrepair and are no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. Caulk of women’s hand sink is in need of repairs. This a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/25/20 and 12/16/19.
2. Trim is not present around the inside dry storage door.
3. Drywall is missing in the storage closet near the bar area/kitchen entrance.
4. Duct tape is being used around the entire kitchen door (also off the hinges and not operational). Cease practice of duct tape as a means of repair - not an approved material.

Number’s 2 and 3 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 6/25/20. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-101.11: (A) Materials indoor shall be SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE. Areas subject to moisture must be Nonabsorbent. (B) In TEMPORARY FOOD ESTABLISHMENT, floor may be material effectively treated to control dust and mud. Walls and ceilings may be material that protects interior from weather and windblown dust and debris. 

(REPEAT) Observed the bar hand sink to be sealed with duct tape. Cease practice. Duct tape is not an approved material for caulking a hand sink. Discussed repairs with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 6/25/20 and 12/16/19.
